title: No-Cook Recipes
subtitle: No heat step means no second chance.
objectives: Explain why no-cook food needs stricter handling
Explain what acid does and does not do
Assemble food so it keeps well

cards.title: No cooking means no second chance
cards.text: Cooking is a kill step: heat removes most of what was there. A no-cook dish has no kill step, so everything depends on what you started with and how you handled it.

cards.title: No kill step changes the rules
points: **Ingredient quality is the whole dish.** Nothing fixes it later.
**Cold stays cold.** The two-hour clock runs the whole time.
**Cross-contamination is unrecoverable.** No heat follows it.
**Wash, chill, assemble last.**

cards.title: Press a temperature
cards.text: Same lab as week 3, and now it matters more. There is no heat step to rescue you.

question.text: Why is handling stricter for a no-cook dish?
options: There is no heat step to kill anything later

cards.title: What acid actually does
cards.text: This one is worth getting right, because people believe the opposite.
points: **Vinegar or calamansi firms the fish** and changes the flavour.
**That looks like cooking. It is not.**
**Acid does not reliably kill bacteria or parasites.**
**Freezing the fish first** is what deals with parasites.

question.text: Does acid in kinilaw make raw fish safe?
options: No — it changes texture, not safety
question.explain: Freezing first is what handles parasites.

cards.title: Build it so it survives until lunch
cards.text: The order you assemble in decides whether it is still good in three hours.
points: **Spread to the edges** — fat is a moisture barrier.
**Wet ingredients in the middle**, dry against the bread.
**Dress a salad at the last moment.** Acid wilts leaves.
**Pack cold things with something cold.**

cards.title: Why astronauts do not eat fresh salad
cards.text: On a long mission, anything that cannot be sterilised or dried is a risk nobody takes.
points: **Fresh produce arrives on resupply** and gets eaten within days.
**Most food is freeze-dried or thermostabilised.**
**No fridge, no shop, no hospital.**
**The no-kill-step problem**, with the stakes raised.

cards.title: What a fighter eats before weighing in
cards.text: Light, cold, no-cook food is exactly what training camps run on.
points: **Fruit, eggs boiled earlier, yoghurt, nuts.**
**Prepared ahead and kept cold.**
**Nothing that needs a stove at 5am.**
**A cool box is part of the kit.**

cards.title: Assembly order is a build order
cards.text: The sequence changes the result even with identical parts.
points: **Same ingredients, different order, different sandwich.**
**Dressing early is a wasted salad.**
**Spread first is armour** against the wet filling.
**Order is a decision**, not an accident.

cards.title: What to remember
points: No cooking means no kill step: ingredients and handling are everything.
Cold stays cold, and the two-hour clock runs throughout.
Acid firms fish and changes flavour; it does not make it safe.
Spread to the edges, wet in the middle, dress at the last moment.

teacher.summary: Term 2 Week 6 TLE. The week is organised around one idea that is rarely said out loud: cooking is a kill step, and a dish without one has different rules. The danger-zone lab from week 3 returns deliberately, because the same mechanism now carries more weight. Kinilaw gets a card and two questions because the belief that acid cooks fish is widespread, specific to this cuisine, and wrong in a way that matters — acid changes texture, freezing handles parasites. Assembly is taught as a build order, with the spread-to-the-edges moisture barrier as the concrete example of why the sequence changes the outcome.
discussion: Ask what a kill step is and which dishes have none.
Ask whether vinegar makes raw fish safe, and what does.
Ask why the spread goes to the edges.
Ask when a salad should be dressed.
extension: Have him build two sandwiches, one spread to the edges and one not, and compare after three hours.
Have him plan a no-cook packed lunch and say how it stays cold.
misconceptions: "Acid cooks fish." It firms it. Freezing deals with parasites.
"No cooking means less to worry about." There is no rescue step.
"Dress the salad early so it soaks in." It wilts.
